skill.displayName: Work Productivity Skillscan Security Workflow Helper

llm.summary: The skill is documentation-only, but it can be auto-invoked for very broad everyday terms, so users should review its scope before installing.

dimensions.detail: No bundled scripts, package installs, command execution, credential access, broad filesystem indexing, or external runtime calls were found; the only URLs are evidence links in documentation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: artifact/agents/openai.yaml enables allow_implicit_invocation, so the broad trigger language may cause the skill to influence conversations without an explicit user request.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The activation scope is overbroad: SKILL.md and related docs list generic triggers such as security, gate, every, must, pass, before, activate, and bug fix, which can match unrelated requests.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism, privilege escalation path, background worker, memory-writing instruction, or tool replacement behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is a workflow helper for SkillScan-style security, reliability, bug-fixing, and adjacent skill-authoring tasks, and the artifacts only provide Markdown/YAML instructions with no executable code.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a general security-workflow helper being auto-selected. Prefer explicit invocation or narrower triggers before using it in environments where unrelated security, bug-fix, or workflow requests could be misrouted.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: Verified: multiple artifacts and the OpenAI agent YAML use broad trigger terms and implicit invocation. This is a real scoping concern, but not evidence of malicious behavior or data access.
[SQP-3] unexpected: Verified: the Chinese README keeps English trigger phrases. This is mainly a localization and user-control concern, not a standalone security issue.
